product.title: 1000 de evenimente care au modelat lumea
product.description: Un nou mod de a privi istoria   De la trecutul îndepărtat până în secolul XXI, această carte prezintă o viziune nouă și actuală a evenimentelor istorice până în ziua de azi. Volumul 1000 de evenimente care au modelat lumea, conceput de National Geographic, prezintă istoria omenirii prin intermediul a șapte capitole fascinante, cu articole numerotate de la 1 la 1000, însoțite de ilustrații superbe, note explicative și relatări ale unor martori oculari. Fiecare capitol începe cu un eseu introductiv, însoțit de o cronologie ilustrativă rezumând momentele importante ale acelei perioade. 1000 de articole individuale prezintă relatări scurte, dar cuprinzătoare, despre evenimente cu rol esențial de-a lungul mileniilor. Cu ajutorul unor coduri de culoare pe fiecare pagină puteți găsi cu ușurință evenimentul dorit.   •400 de ilustrații și alte 20 de eseuri vizuale oferă repere iconografice legate de evenimente-cheie, dezvăluind imagini uimitoare cum este tabloul Guernica de Picasso sau prima schiță grafică a unui atom realizată pe computer. •40 de Conexiuni ne oferă mai multă informație cu privire la modul în care un eveniment a influențat altele de-a lungul timpului: de la apariția miturilor și a picturilor preistorice până la fabricarea banilor și la construirea zgârie-norilor. •300 de Note adaugă o perspectivă unică asupra unui eveniment semnificativ. (știați, de exemplu, că Sfântul Augustin, fondator al teologiei occidentale, s-a născut în Algeria de azi?) •50 de relatări La persoana întâi fac din fiecare cititor un martor ocular al evenimentului istoric respectiv, prin intermediul cuvintelor rostite de regina Elisabeta, de exploratorul Robert Peary, de dictatorul Benito Mussolini, de Eva Hart, o supraviețuitoare din naufragiul Titanicului, de marea apărătoare a drepturilor civile Rosa Parks și de mulți alții.

# The 1000 Events That Shaped the World by Litera

Uncover the sweeping narrative of human history with *The 1000 Events That Shaped the World*. This comprehensive non-fiction volume, conceived by National Geographic and published by Litera, offers an unparalleled and deeply engaging journey through time. From ancient civilizations to modern global events in the 21st century, this book presents a vibrant new perspective on how history has unfolded, detailing pivotal moments that have continually shaped human civilization.

If you are looking for a definitive resource on world history, this collection is designed to satisfy your curiosity, providing not just dates and names, but the context, impact, and personal stories behind the greatest milestones in human existence.

## ð Exploring History Through 1000 Pivotal Moments

The bookâs unique structure allows readers to explore the vast expanse of time without getting lost in dry chronology. The history of humanity is organized across seven fascinating chapters, each providing a deep dive into a specific era. Instead of simply listing facts, *The 1000 Events That Shaped the World* tells interconnected stories through:

**A Global Mosaic of Information:**
*   **1000 Individual Articles:** Each article offers concise yet comprehensive narratives covering events that played an essential role over millennia. You can even use color-coded indices to easily locate the event you are most curious about.
*   **Visual Depth:** Readers will encounter 400 stunning illustrations and 20 visual essays, providing iconic reference pointsâfrom Picasso's *Guernica* to early computer renderings of atoms.
*   **Connecting the Dots (40 Connections):** Learn how events influence each other across time. These sections trace complex connections, spanning from the rise of prehistoric myths and paintings to the development of currency and the construction of modern skyscrapers.
*   **Unique Perspectives (300 Notes):** Gain fascinating "Did You Know?" insights that add layers of depth to significant historical moments, such as learning about Saint Augustine's unexpected birthplace in modern Algeria.

## ðï¸ Becoming a Witness to History: First-Person Accounts

One of the most compelling features is the inclusion of **50 first-person narratives**. These stories cast the reader not merely as an observer, but as a witness to history. Through the powerful words of figures like Queen Elizabeth, explorer Robert Peary, civil rights champion Rosa Parks, and survivors of major events (such as those from the Titanic disaster), you gain an intimate understanding of what these moments felt like.

***The 1000 Events That Shaped the World* is the perfect companion for history enthusiasts, students, or anyone who loves a richly illustrated, narrative-driven journey through time.**

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Q: Is this book suitable for beginners in history?**
A: Yes. The structure is designed to be highly accessible. By breaking down complex eras into 1000 manageable articles, it makes the scope of world history easy and engaging to digest.

**Q: Does the book cover modern history?**
A: Absolutely. While spanning millennia, the narrative extends right up to contemporary events in the 21st century, ensuring a relevant view of how our current world was formed.
